summary: The roughly five-acre waterfront park system of the Pier 70 D4D (Waterfront Terrace, Slipways Commons and Waterfront Promenade, Sections 3.5-3.7) plus the roughly 1,300-foot Pier 70 Shoreline (Section 3.8), to be built by the developer and owned by the Port. Phase 1 includes three acres of parks, but the DDA ties park completion to adjacent buildings and the Port's 2026 report says the Phase 1 parks will be built 'on a schedule that coincides with the delivery of adjacent vertical development', so none has been constructed.

milestones.text: DDA terms approved: parks must be completed 12-18 months after completion of adjacent buildings; the Port Commission must approve the schematic design of each park after review by a design advisory committee; parks are owned and controlled by the Port
Port approves the Phase 1 Submittal, including three acres of parks and backbone infrastructure
Groundbreaking release promises nine acres of new parks and open space, with Phase 1 parks and first buildings anticipated in 2021-2022

Phase 1 streets and utilities accepted by the City and Port; 'the balance of the Phase 1 horizontal improvements, largely comprised of the Phase 1 parks and open space', deferred to coincide with adjacent vertical development
Proposed DDA amendments would 'better align open spaces with revised vertical development schedule'

facts.value: 3.5 Waterfront Terrace, 3.6 Slipways Commons, 3.7 Waterfront Promenade, 3.8 Pier 70 Shoreline (zones 1-4 of Figure 3.4.1)
waterfront area approximately 5.0 acres; shoreline approximately 1,300 linear feet; nine acres of public open space project-wide
Bay Trail, Building 6 viewing pavilion, social lawn, picnic terrace, shoreline path; views of ship-repair activity to the north
Connects the historic node of Buildings 2, 12 and 21 to the Bay: Bay Trail, multifunction commons with lawn and cafe terraces, event plaza, craneway piers, craneway viewing pavilion, shoreline path

Bay Trail, outdoor dining terraces, seating promenade, shoreline path, craneway piers, 22nd Street viewing pavilion, tree grove; seating in lieu of buildings at the water 'anticipates long-term changes in the shoreline'
Design must orient to views, provide multiple access points to the water, and adapt to wave conditions and sea level rise in coordination with BCDC, the Army Corps and the Port (S3.8.1-3.8.3)
James Corner Field Operations (D4D project team)
Port of San Francisco; the Chief Harbor Engineer calendars acceptance of each park parcel at the Port Commission
three acres of parks in the Phase 1 Submittal; the Port's 2026 Exhibit A draws the Phase 1 boundary around the waterfront open space east of Building 12 and Parcel E2 (the Slipways Commons area)
The site is being raised to protect against flooding and sea level rise (Port's 2026 report); the 2018 groundbreaking release described Building 12 as elevated 9 feet for sea-level-rise protection

open_questions: No Port Commission schematic-design approval for any of the four waterfront open spaces was found on 2018-2026 agendas, so none appears to have reached that stage.
Which named spaces make up the three Phase 1 acres is not stated; the reading of Exhibit A above (Slipways Commons area in Phase 1) is this project's interpretation of a diagram.

Cost of the parks: the 2017 memo gives $260.5 million of eligible horizontal costs for all three phases but no park line item was extracted; the Phase 1 infrastructure Notice of Completion (Nov 2022) was described as a $150 million investment without a park breakdown.

Interim use: the Elevation Sky Park venue occupies waterfront land near 22nd Street for up to five years; whether it sits on future park land or only on parcels E3/H2 is unresolved (see the E3 record).
